Compare fitted allocations across model and input specifications

Source: R/07-allocation_compare.R
compare_allocations.Rd

Summarizes several fitted allocations side by side: regional contact, attributed capacity and its per-contact value, the spread of contact across origins, agreement between predicted and observed counts, and the fitted loss. Each fit's coverage is computed from its saved outputs; nothing is refitted.

Usage

compare_allocations(
  fits,
  models = NULL,
  reference = 1L,
  zones = NULL,
  coverage_args = list()
)

# S3 method for class 'ae_allocation_comparison'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ae_allocation_comparison'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  type = c("fits", "zones"),
  ...
)

Arguments

fits

A named list of ae_multistart_fit results from fit_allocation(), each with a selected fit. An element can instead be a result of spax() that fitted a model; it supplies its fit and its model. A result that was evaluated at given values has no fit and is refused.

models

Optional named list of the corresponding models from clm_allocation(), with the same names, used to verify that travel times are identical before reporting loss differences. The elements of fits that are results of spax() bring their own models and must not be named here. When fits mixes results with plain fits, give models for the plain ones.

reference

Name or position of the reference fit.

zones

Optional data frame with origin_id and zone columns covering every fitted origin.

coverage_args

Named reporting controls passed to the coverage calculation for every fit, such as norm, rho_floor, contact_need_floor, contact_cut and adequacy_cut.

x

An ae_allocation_comparison.

digits

Significant digits for printed values.

...

Unused.

row.names, optional

Standard as.data.frame() arguments; unused.

type

"fits" for one row per fit or "zones" for zone summaries.

Value

An ae_allocation_comparison with a table (one row per fit), a long zones table when zones are supplied, and the reference name. Use print() or as.data.frame(type = "fits") / as.data.frame(type = "zones").

Details

Loss differences from the reference are reported only when the comparison is like for like: the same observed targets, loss function and arguments (Poisson fits: the same floor, a fit that stored none used 1e-9, or floors that change neither loss), demand, supply, origin and facility IDs and prepared travel times. Travel times are checked only when models are supplied, and each model must reproduce its own fit; otherwise loss differences are left missing. Fits of models with demand groups (prepare_allocation()) are comparable only with each other, with the same group IDs and, once models are supplied, the same demand and the same travel times for every group; a shared-parameter fit and a by_group fit on the same group-labelled target answer whether the group decays differ. The table then shows the free parameters, such as sigma.<group>, and coverage comes from the pooled outputs. Contact and capacity values remain comparable across specifications, but they are conditional on each specification's inputs.

For fits to the outside-count outputs (flow_outside, utilization_outside, utilization_outside_by_group), the count_correlation is over the whole target, the "(outside)" cells included, so it is not comparable with the correlation of a fit to facility counts without outside counts. The capacity-only comparator of check_allocation() applies to facility totals without outside counts only.

With zones, each fit is also summarized by zone using contact-weighted aggregation, and the zones whose reporting class differs from the reference are listed. Classes require an adequacy cut in coverage_args; each fit uses its own regional contact as the contact cut unless contact_cut is given.
